app.subtitle: Would a simpler strategy have done better with your money? Hindsight replays your own deposits and withdrawals in an alternative, such as an index ETF, Bitcoin or a fixed mix: each deposit buys it on the same day, each withdrawal sells some of it. The method is known as a Public Market Equivalent (Long–Nickels).
app.realUnavailable: No inflation data, so no real figures.

table.realNote: Real figures use purchasing power at the end of the period: only gain and MWR change. The end value stays the same, and so does the gain difference (both gains share the same deposits and withdrawals; only an uncovered withdrawal counts at end-of-period purchasing power).
table.maxDrawdownInfo: Largest fall from a previous high, time-weighted: deposits and withdrawals are neither gains nor losses. For an alternative it is the asset's own price fall in your base currency, whatever the simulation held; for your portfolio the fall of what you actually held, from Wealthfolio's daily valuations. Nominal in both views. Wealthfolio's Performance page computes it the same way; it differs when the accounts differ (a cash account, for example, dampens the fall). Hover a figure for the dates of the high and the low.
table.ddUnavailable: Your portfolio's drawdown needs a valuation of every selected account on each booking day; Wealthfolio's history has a gap there.

shortfall.title: Uncovered withdrawal
shortfall.p1: This alternative was worth less than a withdrawal; only the covered part counts. Compare the gain, not the end value.

lateStart.title: Late start
lateStart.p1: No prices before this date. The money stays uninvested until then and is bought at once.
lateStart.partial: A component has no prices before this date. Its share of every deposit stays uninvested until then and is bought at once; the rest of the mix is invested as usual.

info.mwrPeriod: Money-weighted return over the period (XIRR), not annualised.
info.start: Your portfolio's value at the start of the period. Every line starts with it, as if it were deposited on that day; deposits are the bookings after it.
info.bookings: The count is original bookings in the period. Amounts are netted per day; alternatives only include covered withdrawals.
info.vs: This alternative's gain minus your portfolio's gain, with the same deposits and withdrawals on the same days. It equals the difference in end value unless the alternative could not fully cover a withdrawal: then it is lower by the uncovered amount (in real figures, that amount at end-of-period purchasing power).

mix.title: Create a mix
mix.description: Each deposit is split by the weights, each withdrawal sells all assets pro rata. Yearly rebalancing resets the weights on the first trading day of each year.
mix.name: Name
mix.hintAssets: Choose an asset for every row.
mix.hintSum: The weights add up to {{sum}} %, not 100 %.
mix.hintInvalid: Every weight must be above 0 with at most two decimals, and every asset different.
mix.hintDuplicate: This mix is already in the list.

guide.shows1: Gain difference: the alternative's gain minus yours. Above zero, it would have earned more with exactly your deposits and withdrawals.
guide.shows2: MWR p.a.: each line's money-weighted yearly return (XIRR) on the same cash flows; below a year, over the period. It is the same comparison as a rate: unless a withdrawal was not covered, the line with the higher gain has the higher MWR.
guide.shows3: Value chart: each line's value over time; the dashed “Net in” line is the money paid in minus the money taken out up to that day.
guide.shows4: Difference chart: each line's gain minus your portfolio's on that day, the gain being the value minus the money that line took in and paid out, so deposits cause no jumps. Your portfolio is the zero line; above it, the alternative was ahead by then. Today's point is the gain difference.
guide.shows5: Max drawdown: the largest fall from a previous high, time-weighted, so deposits and withdrawals count as neither gain nor loss: for an alternative on its price, for your portfolio on Wealthfolio's daily valuations. It shows how bumpy the ride was, not which did better.
guide.shows6: Real: gain and MWR in purchasing power at the end of the period, by the OECD consumer price index of your time zone's country (else your base currency's). Values and the gain difference stay the same.
guide.assumes1: Before taxes and fees: the alternatives pay none; your portfolio includes those actually paid.
guide.assumes2: A deposit buys at the adjusted closing price (Yahoo Finance) of its day or the next trading day, a withdrawal sells that amount. Distributions are reinvested.
guide.assumes3: A withdrawal larger than the alternative's value only counts as far as it was covered.
guide.assumes4: Before an asset's first price the money stays uninvested and is bought at once on that day.
guide.assumes5: Only money flowing in from outside counts, not transfers between the selected accounts.
guide.assumes6: Asset transfers from outside count at the booking's price, else at the Wealthfolio price around that day. Worthless ones (e.g. spam tokens) are ignored.
guide.assumes7: A period starting after your first deposit begins with your portfolio's value that day as a deposit.
guide.assumes8: A mix splits each deposit by its weights and sells pro rata; “Yearly” resets the weights on the first day of the year on which every asset has a price. Its drawdown is the strategy's (one unit invested at the start), not the simulated position's.
